chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Habib ibn Hakim, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the least form of al-ilhad (deviation/ straying), so he said: Pride (al-kibr) is from it.

key_terms.الْإِلْحَادِ: Deviation or straying from the correct path, often used in the context of supplication or prayer.
key_terms.الْكُبْرُ: Pride or arrogance, identified here as the source of deviation.

ai.seo_question: What is the least form of deviation (ilhad) in worship according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies pride (*al-kibr*) as the minimal degree of *al-ilhad*, a term often associated with subtle deviations in supplication or theological understanding. This highlights pride not merely as a vice, but as the foundational spiritual flaw that leads one astray from divine guidance, a concept deeply resonant with the Shia emphasis on humility before God.
